verdict.rationale: GrowthBook documents a first-party GrowthBook Proxy that runs next to your app, caches SDK payloads, and keeps serving flags if the API is down. It also adds streaming and remote evaluation, and GrowthBook itself can be fully self-hosted. Keeping SDK traffic inside your network is implied by co-locating the proxy rather than stated outright. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the proxy keeps serving during a vendor outage, explicit documentation of network-isolated or private-network proxy deployment.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can run a relay/edge proxy so flags stay served when the vendor is unreachable and SDK traffic stays inside my network

citations.quote: Run the GrowthBook Proxy next to your app to cache SDK payloads, reduce latency, and keep serving flags if the API is down.
It turbocharges your GrowthBook implementation by providing speed, scalability, security, and real-time feature rollouts.
Run GrowthBook on your own infrastructure with Docker Compose, including MongoDB, the API, and the front-end.
